meta.parties: Nagamma v. Sathappa Chetty Et Al

rules.statement: Under Roman-Dutch law, the omission of property from a will does not necessarily mean it is disposed of by the will. Instead, such property may descend as ab intestato to those nearest in blood to the testator.
rules.supporting_quote: "According to Van Leeuwen the principle stated in Voet (lib, 28, tit. 1, n. 1) that it was not according to law unumquemque qui testandi jus habet etiam pro parte testatum et pro parte intestatum mori posse was never adopted in the Roman-Dutch Law. In that law it appears to be the rule that if a testator excludes part of his property from the operation of his will, it descends as ab intestato, and not to the instituted heirs."
